svg.title: TOPAK C7 — A Thinker learns its tools from the mechanism, and the allowlist entry has one schema
svg.desc: ADR-0049 states the allowlist entry once: five parts, keyed name@digest, each field marked checked or claimed, with ten load checks a bundle must pass to load at all. The entry is the one statement of a Run tool's channel: the tool host reads the target there (ADR-0034 A2, R4; ADR-0033 A9). ADR-0048 makes every entry carry an interface, and at grant the mechanism renders the tool list of the lease's revision, delivers it to the Thinker and opens the round's topic with it, so an Observer is given what its Thinker was told. The list is the only description with standing, and Run's ingress becomes a closed list of four. Both ratified in Batch 34; two conditions were restated first, W10 (G10 result 3) and a list narrowed to one tool, which a lease cannot carry (result 4).
svg.text: TOPAK · C7

text.tspan: A Thinker learns its tools from the mechanism, and the allowlist entry has one schema

svg.text: ADR-0049 states the allowlist entry once: five parts, keyed name@digest, each field marked checked or claimed, with ten load checks a bundle must pass to load at all. The entry is the one statement of a Run tool's channel: the tool host reads the target there (ADR-0034 A2, R4; ADR-0033 A9). ADR-0048 makes every entry carry an interface, and at grant the mechanism renders the tool list of the lease's revision, delivers it to the Thinker and opens the

round's topic with it, so an Observer is given what its Thinker was told. The list is the only description with standing, and Run's ingress becomes a closed list of four. Both ratified in Batch 34; two conditions were restated first, W10 (G10 result 3) and a list narrowed to one tool, which a lease cannot carry (result 4).

text.tspan: Accepted · C4, C3 · Batch 34, at R6
Accepted · C4; C2 for §5 · Batch 34, at R4
Built at reference · ADR-0033 A9 (B32), A10 (B34), A15 (B35)

svg.text: No seat gains a variant. G10 item 59 discharged; item 84 closed.

text.tspan: One entry, read three ways: by the tool host, by the renderer, and by the admit path

svg.text: Entries keyed name@digest, each for one domain, signed with the bundle
(ADR-0044) and promoted with it.
Beside them (ADR-0049 §7): labels.vocabulary, labels.delivery per seat kind,
labels.root.
Every bundle was in the old form: the move was a bundle change and a policy
change together (policies/data.json, A10).

text.tspan: The issued rules: two lists (ADR-0025 §1 (h), A2)

svg.text: Targets inside the deployment: an entry reaching one is not outward.
Entries allowed to release a reserved label, by name and digest.
Each widens what a bundle may declare, so adding to either is an issuance. With
neither issued, every entry with a channel is outward and none may release a
reserved name.
Since A15 the rules' well-formedness reads them (a releaser named by name and
digest; an inside target not empty); the rules floor bounds neither (ADR-0026 is not
amended).

text.tspan: At load: W1 to W10, or the bundle does not load

svg.text: Made by the mechanism at load, after the signature and before any decision
counts (ADR-0030 A2).
Checks on the data's shape; no judgment. Each refusal names its check (
allowlist.rs check).
A bundle cannot waive them, an issuance does not change them: a
mechanism constant, changed only by a release. They are harder to change
than the floor.
W7 and W9 read the inside-target list; W8 reads the releasers. The full table is
below.
read once, at load
Kept per bundle revision; a grant names the revision, so a call is
decided against the revision its lease names and the key it carries
outward is derived and never declared: a channel whose target the
issued rules do not list as inside (§4). A bundle cannot mark its own
entry as inside.
A new bundle reaches a principal at its next grant (ADR-0031 R2):
the list and the decisions cannot change inside a round.
well-formed
not well-formed: refused, every reason named
Of the bundle revision the lease names, and from nowhere else. Node configuration says where a
module is and what its bytes are, and states no channel: one declaration, nothing to disagree with
it.
A hosted tool whose entry declares no channel in that revision is not run (ADR-0033 A9, B32).

text.tspan: 2 · At grant, the mechanism renders the tool list

svg.text: Every entry of the revision for the seat's domain that the lease may call, and no other, in one
fixed form, mechanical and total: a syntactic lift (ADR-0007). No admit.
name and digest checked on every call; domain (an Invoke of a Run entry, an Actuate of a
Build entry, refused); type and required in the bundle tier; a handle's label against accepts.

text.tspan: A Wasm tool with one network capability: a connection to that target

svg.text: No other socket; any other import refused before it runs. The capability binds the target; the protocol (kind) is
recorded and not enforced. At the reference a core module, not a component (PROVISIONAL tool-abi, I44). A
native tool's target stays an assertion (G19).

text.tspan: The round topic's opening record, and the Thinker

svg.text: Written before any other record, before the session exists: kind open, the list's digest and the bundle revision in its
envelope, the list in its payload; no admit and no sequence number (ADR-0042 A1; I45). If it cannot be written no
session is opened; a launched guest is destroyed.
The Thinker gets the same list with its token; topak mcp passes it in its instructions; a session may ask again (
ToolList), with no admit and the same answer all round. An Observer reads it under W(p); its mark does not
assert it read it.
A call the list did not name is refused at the allowlist, and every attempt is an ordinary admit (ToldMatchesDecided,
below).

text.tspan: §2: the digest, and what it does not cover

svg.text: An entry's digest is the SHA-256 of the tool artifact's digest joined with the canonical form of the entry's inputs part, re-checked on every call: a change to the artifact or to an input is a new key.
It does not cover the interface, the labels or the channel: declarations about the tool, fixed by the bundle's revision and signature. A corrected description is a promotion, not a new tool.

Not followed at the reference (R4; G10 item 94; I13): it digests the schema the tool's own MCP server reports, and a Wasm tool's digest is its module's bytes alone. Nothing compares either with the entry's inputs. Carried as a debt; not among §9's conditions.

text.tspan: §6: what makes a bundle's allowlist well-formed (the full table); at the reference each is seen with a bundle built to fail it

svg.text: An entry's key is not its name and digest, or its domain is missing
An input lacks type or required, or the type is not one of the three
purpose is empty, an input has no note, or either is over the size bound
The bound is a mechanism parameter; its values are the reference's: 1,024 bytes for purpose, 256 for a note (I33)
A Run entry has no channel, or a channel lacks kind or target
A Build entry has a channel
ADR-0022 §3's hermeticity obligation as a check on the data (A3)
A Run entry has no result.label, or any label name is outside the bundle's vocabulary
The reference applies it to the root, accepts and the delivery table too
An outward entry's result.label lacks untrusted
ADR-0047 F4
Reads the inside-target list
result.releases holds a reserved name and the issued rules do not name the entry
ADR-0047 F5
Reads the releaser list
An outward entry takes inputs and marks none as a destination, without saying it has none
ADR-0047 F6
destinations: none at the entry's top level, so an omission and a decision look different
An entry or an input carries a field this record does not define, or a Build entry carries any of the labels part (R4). First written: accepts or destination on an input the entry does not have

Restated before ratification (G10 §3, result 3): in the entry's own form accepts and destination sit inside the input they describe, so the first W10 could not be failed. A misspelt or misplaced field is now not silently
dropped

ADR-0047 F6
The delivery table has no row for thinker or for observer, or a row is not total over the vocabulary
No row is asked for emergency: a person on an emergency seat is then given handles (G10 result 6; item 92)

W7 to W9 are how ADR-0047's F4 to F6 are checked (R1): ADR-0047 §7 says what must be refused and why; this table is the definitive form. Seven of the entry's fields are claims, bounded in three places by these checks (finding 1): the allowlist is where a deployment's honesty is concentrated.

Run's ingress is a closed list of four (ADR-0043 A1; ADR-0042 A1). Two ratified records had said three, and "nothing else": the list stays closed and the sentence changes,
which is why ADR-0048 is C3 on the drafter's reading. In Build the list is the task, the admitted Read content and the tool list (ADR-0037 A2), and a Build round's list is ingress
and consumed for lineage (ADR-0035 R6, Proposed). Labels on each: C6.

text.tspan: §3: the mechanism's list is the only description with standing

svg.text: A Thinker's tools are the ones on its list, named as the list names them; the list supplies the name and digest an Actuate or Invoke must carry.
What a Persona, a task or a consulted object says about a tool is content: the mechanism does not read it and no admit turns on it. A task says what to do; the list
says what there is to do it with.
No tool supplies text at run time, so the MCP "rug-pull" cannot happen; a description carrying an injection now has to pass promotion. Promoting a tool no longer
makes a Persona stale.
Purpose text is still a claim: a tool described as read-only that writes is detected by nothing here (§5).

§4: how it changes. Promotion is as strong as its gates, and at the reference gate evidence is an operator's assertion (G10 §8).

text.tspan: A lease cannot be narrowed to a tool (R6; G10 result 4, item 95)

svg.text: §2 says the list is the allowlist "narrowed by that lease". ADR-0031 §1's lease schema is closed and carries no tool set, so the behaviour first asked for, "a lease
narrowed to one tool is given a list of one", could not be shown.
What is shown: a lease whose alphabet lacks the variant that names a tool is given a list of none, and a list holds only entries the deployment's allowlist admits. At the
reference the narrowing is the parameters' tools for the domain when the alphabet holds Invoke or Actuate (I45).

text.tspan: Whether a lease should carry a tool set is ADR-0031's question, left open.
): 27 TLC rows; five properties proved, 215 obligations, certified

svg.text: Under a live lease the Thinker was told the allowlist of the granted revision, narrowed by the lease: no more and no fewer
No admitted call names a tool the Thinker was not told of, and no call is refused for one it was told of: over what it was
actually told (ghost)
Under a live lease, what the Thinker was told is what it was told at the grant
No effect is recorded on a round's topic before its opening record
The list in the opening record is the list the Thinker was told: the Observer reads what the Thinker was given
Two bundle revisions with different allowlists (revision 1 allows t1, t2; revision 2 allows t2, t3), so that a promotion in the middle of a round changes which tools exist. The Thinker is havoc: it
calls any tool, told or not. One principal, any number of rounds. The lease's narrowing is modelled as any set of tools, which ADR-0031's lease does not carry (R6). Not modelled: the rendering and
its size bound; purpose text; every reason for refusal other than the allowlist.
All five proved, with no assumption: 215 obligations (ADR-0048 R4).
Certified (ADR-0046 A1): 133 closed by the prover's normalization, 75 by SMT with a proof the ethos checker accepted, 7 temporal steps by LS4, which no checker confirms.
The module found no fault in the record. ToolListIsExact alone is a function of the grant; what a model can test is a round in which a bundle is promoted.
A certified proof is not a verified one. At the reference the module is tied by tests (e2e the_tool_list_is_delivered_and_opens_the_round), by no trace; the binding table has no row
for it (G10 item 90).

text.tspan: What the reference does not follow, of records in force (G10 item 94)

svg.text: ADR-0049 §2's digest over the entry's inputs: the reference digests what the tool's own server reports, or a Wasm module's bytes (I13).
The two issued lists are read once, from the genesis rules, when bundles load: an issuance that changes them does not re-check a bundle already loaded (I46; ADR-0033 A15).
Also open: two comments under policies/ still call ADR-0049 Proposed, and a comment there is part of the bundle's revision (item 98).

D-0048-1: the tool list not delivered; a Thinker learns its tools from its Persona, its task or a consulted object. Falsifies: a Thinker's description of a tool is bound to the entry's name and digest.
Voids no theorem; no type change. The reference until 2026.10.05.
ADR-0049 adds none: an entry that lacks a part is the degeneracy of the record that asks for it (D-0047-1, D-0048-1, D-0034-5, D-0034-6).
holds (514 states)

At the reference (Annex B): T-0045-34 has an instance since 2026.10.05, and the list's rendering is the reference's own (I45). T-0045-24 is still excluded there, for a reason that ended with ADR-0033 A9: the target is now read from the entry, not from node configuration, and moving the row is ADR-0045's to do (G10 item 89). A Wasm tool there is a core module, not a component (I44). One hand: both records drafted 2026.10.03, built and ratified 2026.10.05; not reviewed by a reader other than the drafter (ADR-0029 A2.5; G10 §8).
